reference.title: Barbell Curtsey Lunge
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you step back and lower, exhale as you drive back to standing.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s step and lower, short pause, about 1.5 s up and step in

prescription.tempo: Controlled: about 1 s down, short pause, 1 s up
prescription.load: Start light; balance under the bar comes first.
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep is steady.

cues.text: Bar on the upper traps just below the bony bump at the base of the neck, hands just outside the shoulders, elbows down, shoulder blades squeezed. Stand tall, feet hip width.
Step the right foot back and across behind the left, landing on the ball of the foot; hips and bar stay square to the front.
Bend both knees straight down until the front knee is about 90 degrees; front knee over the foot, chest up under the bar.
Drive through the front heel to stand and step the right foot back beside the left; breathe out as you rise.
Stand tall, re-brace and repeat or switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Hips and bar twisting toward the back leg
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones and the bar facing forward; step less far across.
Push the front knee out over the middle toes.
Stay tall with the bar level; lighten the load.
Step far enough back that both knees can bend to about 90 degrees.

kinematics.peak: Right ball of the foot 60 cm behind and 18 cm past the left ankle (crossing the midline)
kinematics.norm: Back foot lands behind and across the front foot (reference movement); no study gives a step length for the curtsy lunge (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: ≈91°, 21.4 cm above the floor (knee joint centre)
kinematics.norm: Lowers behind the front heel without touching the floor (clinical opinion)
The back thigh crosses the midline (reference movement; clinical opinion)
Upright to slightly forward; trunk lean shifts work toward the hip extensors (Farrokhi 2008)

kinematics.peak: Step back 0.8 s, 1.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 0.75 s up, step in 0.8 s
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1-2 s down and 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Curtsey Lunge, video (movement reference only)

cautions: Unrack the bar from a squat rack (J-hooks at about mid-chest height) and re-rack it after the set; set the safeties or use a spotter.
Keep the bar on the muscle of the upper back, never on the neck.
Knee pain on the crossing leg: step less far across.
Balance is harder with the load high on the back: master the dumbbell version first.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shorter, less crossed step while learning.

muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front (standing) leg hip extensor; in the reverse lunge gluteus maximus was more active in the stationary limb than in the stepping limb (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front (standing) leg hip extensor; in the reverse lunge gluteus maximus was more active in the stationary limb than in the stepping limb (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors lower and raise the body; rectus femoris was more active in the stepping limb in the reverse lunge (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors lower and raise the body; rectus femoris was more active in the stepping limb in the reverse lunge (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Front-leg hip abductor resists the knee caving in as the back leg crosses behind; in the reverse lunge only the stationary-limb gluteus medius reached a strengthening level (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Front-leg hip abductor resists the knee caving in as the back leg crosses behind; in the reverse lunge only the stationary-limb gluteus medius reached a strengthening level (Hoogenboom 2024).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Work on both legs to steady the crossed stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Work on both legs to steady the crossed stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension on the front leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension on the front leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the hips and shoulders square to the front (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the pelvis twisting toward the crossing leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the pelvis twisting toward the crossing leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: The muscle shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: The muscle shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.
